prerequisites: Prior knowledge of drawing, equivalent to Scientific-Technological Baccalaureate studies.

learning_outcomes.text: Know, understand, and apply a set of knowledge about the fundamentals and standardization of industrial engineering drawing, in its broadest sense, while promoting the development of spatial ability.
Acquire the ability for abstract reasoning and the establishment of efficient strategies and procedures in solving graphic problems within the context of engineering works and projects.
Use graphical communication among technicians, by creating and interpreting plans according to Technical Drawing Standards, implying the use of new technologies.
Adopt a favorable attitude towards lifelong learning in the profession, being proactive, participatory, and with a spirit of self-improvement.

syllabus_topics: Block I. Plane Geometry. Review of prior knowledge. Metric geometry applied to engineering. Technical curves.

Block II. 2D and 3D Computer-Aided Design. Introduction to Computer-Aided Design (CAD). Working environment. Coordinate Systems. UCS-SCP Change. UCSFOLLOW. ADMINSCP. Drawing Commands. Graphic Entities. Drawing Aids. Entity References. Basic Elements - Editing, Repetition Commands, Expression tools: layers and hatching. Visualization, Presentation, Dimensioning, Scaling and Printing Commands. 3D Environments: Basic Operations, Modeling, Assemblies, Plans. Information exchange.

Block III. Representation Systems. Fundamentals Introduction: Types of projections. Projective invariants. Dihedral System. Fundamentals. Belonging and Incidence. Parallelism and Perpendicularity. Distances, Angles. Operations: Rotations, Plane Changes, and Rebatements. Surfaces. Polyhedral Radiated and Revolution. Systems of dimensioned planes. Fundamentals. Belonging and Incidence. Parallelism and Perpendicularity. Distances, Angles. Rebatements. Belonging and Incidence. Parallelism and Perpendicularity. Distances, Angles. Operations: Rotations, Plane Changes, and Rebatements. Axonometric System: Fundamentals. Types of axonometries: trimetric, dimetric, and isometric. Cavalier Perspective System: Fundamentals. Conical Perspective System: Fundamentals.

assessment_methods.method: Problems or exercises delivered during the semester (paper and CAD formats)

assessment_rules: For continuous assessment, two partial exams each count 35% and require a minimum of 4.0/10, with a 5.0/10 average. Two practical lab components (general CAD test and practical assignments) each count 15% and require a minimum of 5.0/10. Overall, a 5.0/10 average in theory and 5.0/10 in practicals are needed to pass. Students failing continuous assessment or opting out must take a final exam covering all content, divided into two theoretical/practical parts, each requiring a minimum of 4.0/10 and a combined average of 5.0/10, plus a practical test (CAD + layout) where each part needs a minimum of 5.0/10. A similar resit exam is held in June-July for all students who have not passed.
